text:
[IRET.7.5.1] **`linear_scan: false` overlay — the equality anchor is
extracted at load.** When the loaded DSC was compiled with
`linear_scan: false`, every positive beta node's join-test list contains at
least one EQ test of the form `BINOP(EQ, VAR(left, i, j), VAR(right, k))`.
For a positive node, the beta node loader must:

1. Extract `(fact_idx=i, left_slot=j, right_slot=k)` from this test
   and store it in the beta node's `lmem_idx_*` and `ralpha_idx_*`
   fields.
2. Compile a specialized comparator over (token, fact) that performs
   a direct typed comparison on slots `t->facts[i]->slots[j]` and
   `f->slots[k]` without calling the expression evaluator.
3. Use this comparator in place of `join_tests_pass` for the equality-
   anchor check during index probe.  Remaining join tests still use
   `join_tests_pass`.

An EQ join test of that form is a legal anchor, wherever it stands in the
list, when it is **decided**: both slots are non-nullable and the comparison
cannot raise by their declared types. A decided anchor answers only `true` or
`false`, and join tests combine as an absorbing `and` ([IRET.7.6], [LNUL.4.2]),
so probing on it first changes neither whether the pair passes nor the fault
the pair yields. An anchor that could answer `null` or raise could change both —
for a negated join, whether it blocks — so the loader must not probe on one.
The guarantee is for an artefact that does not lie about a slot's type
([LDET.1.11]).

The loader takes the first such test as the anchor. A negated node has no
anchor and no index ([LNLS.5.8]).

This reduces the join-test hot-path cost from O(E) to O(1) for the
equality anchor. [LNLS.5.1]'s both-directions O(1) bound needs more than
this: an index over a whole composite identity, and one on negated nodes.

This supplements, and does not replace, the base [IRET.7.5]
behaviour. It is a `must` on the reference engine's loader, naming
this engine's own fields, so the implementation tree is where it
belongs.

alloy.name: iret_7_5_1__v5_null_anchor_escapes
alloy.note: WHY THE ANCHOR MUST BE NON-NULL: a null anchor is in no bucket, where the whole `where` is null and blocks the `no` pattern ([LNUL.4.7]).

alloy.name: rlow_5_5__v5_hoist_sound
alloy.note: HOISTING AND PROBING ARE SOUND for an artefact that does not lie: filters on decided conjuncts leave the decision of a positive and of a `no` pattern, and the record, unchanged. Admitting a nullable filter breaks it (TEETH). V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.
